# Baldur's Gate 3最近几个月口碑有什么变化？是哪次更新导致的？玩家在抱怨什么？

在2026年8月至11月期间，《博德之门3》的整体口碑依然保持着极高评价，其合作战役、个性鲜明的同伴、高交互性以及丰富的选择和对话受到广泛赞誉 [R82][R83][R84]。在此期间，游戏并没有发布任何官方更新或补丁；开发商此前已于2025年7月宣布补丁8（Patch 8）为最后一个重大更新，团队随后转向新游戏的开发 [R131]。因此，最近几个月的玩家口碑和人数波动并非由特定的新更新导致。在玩家人数方面，游戏的Steam平均在线人数在2026年8月达到峰值后，于9月和10月出现了明显的持续下滑 [R77][R78][R79]。

### **时间线**

*   **2025年7月31日**：开发商发布“Room Temperature Fix #33”，并宣布补丁8（Patch 8）是最后一个重大游戏更新 [R131]。
*   **2025年9月23日**：发布热修复#34（Hotfix #34），引入了原生的Steam Deck版本以提升稳定性、缩短加载时间并使运行更流畅 [R133]。
*   **2025年12月1日**：官方确认2025年内已推出包括12个新子职业、完整跨平台联机支持和拍照模式在内的“最终最后一个补丁” [R135]。
*   **2026年3月26日**：发布热修复#36（Hotfix #36），解决此前因修复损坏存档而引入的性能问题、崩溃和卡死现象 [R136]。
*   **2026年6月**：Steam平均在线人数为39,517人，峰值人数68,855人 [R75]。
*   **2026年7月**：Steam平均在线人数升至44,808人，峰值人数78,225人（环比增长13.39%） [R76]。
*   **2026年8月**：Steam平均在线人数达到49,972人，峰值人数为83,011人（环比增长11.53%） [R77]。
*   **2026年9月**：Steam平均在线人数降至42,932人，峰值人数为76,065人（环比减少14.09%） [R78]。
*   **2026年10月**：Steam平均在线人数降至38,530人，峰值人数降至71,090人（环比减少10.25%） [R79]。

### **玩家在抱怨什么**

在2026年8月6日至11月6日期间，给出负面评价的玩家主要抱怨游戏的剧情、角色设计、第一幕进度缓慢、技术问题、较差的用户体验（UX），以及后期玩法的重复与枯燥 [R93][R95][R96]。部分非龙与地下城（D&D）粉丝的玩家也表示难以对游戏产生兴趣 [R98]。

以下是部分玩家的真实评价：
*   一位游玩时间为87.8小时的玩家批评角色设定过于造作：
    > *"Honestly, I've had this game since release and I just can't with it. All of the characters are so goddamn cringe I cannot stand the story long enough to make it past the first act. It's like being stuck with a bunch of hypersexual theater kids..."* [R95]
*   另一位游玩了38.8小时的玩家也因同样的原因未能通关第一幕：
    > *"Nearly 40 hours put into the game and I can't get through the first Act, not because of difficulty, but because I just don't like the characters or the story enough to care about any of it."* [R93]
*   一位游玩了200.9小时的玩家指出了游戏在发售三年后依然存在技术问题：
    > *"Buy only at deep discount if you're a CRPG fan. Accolades and the community's abusive attachment disorder aside, this is a still painfully janky game three years after release."* [R92]

### **数据无法回答的问题**

*   **更新对玩家人数的影响**：由于在2026年8月1日至11月6日期间没有发布任何官方更新、补丁或公告，数据无法解释该阶段的玩家人数波动是否与更新有关。
*   **11月的玩家趋势**：由于缺乏2026年11月的历史数据，无法提供该月完整的玩家人数变化趋势。
*   **平台局限性**：本报告数据仅基于Steam平台的评价与SteamCharts在线人数，无法反映PlayStation 5等主机平台的数据。
*   **统计局限性**：Steam评论仅反映了撰写评论的玩家群体，SteamSpy的所有者数量属于估算值，且开发者的动机仅能根据官方公告中“转向下一款游戏开发”的陈述来了解 [R131]。

Yeah, yeah, I know, I must be crazy... But I just really didn't like it, OK? I'm sad to be this disappointed.

It's a well-made game for sure, no doubt about it. If it weren't for the great expectations, there might not have been such a great disappointment. I've enjoyed Larian's previous works, loved them even, but there was almost nothing about BG3 to inspire similar feelings.

The story was boilerplate D&D plot, stretched to 100+ hours. Meaningless, emotionless, drawn out tropes and cliches. Only Act 2 made me feel something. I put off wrapping up Act 3 for years from sheer boredom, and felt nothing but tedium by the end.

The characters were as uninteresting as they were horny, I couldn't care about them with the obvious exception of Karlach, who was an actually well-written character. Shadowheart and Astarion were ok-ish. The rest were forgettable. Couldn't decide if the late shoehorning of Jaheira and Minsc was welcome fanservice or a way to distract from the voidness Gale, Wyll and Halsin.

The 5e ruleset is not a good fit for such a game, and Larian's attempts at patching it, while valiant, were not sufficient. Some made it actively worse. The combat was plodding, the interface clunky and annoying, the abilities and items both overwhelming in number and underwhelming in the choices they presented. 5e was never meant to be a lootfest, but the magic items the game showered you with created perverse incentives and boring micromanagement. The gear-juggling was made so much worse by the abysmal stash and inventory system. That they were this bad really boggles the mind.

In the end, the game had nothing to say, nothing to offer but a fun romp that degraded into tedium by the end, Almost nothing about this game is truly memorable, artistically profound or genuinely touching. It was a 150 hour fast food meal served on a really nice and shiny plate. For all its bugs and failures, I will forever remember and cherish Owlcat's glorious mess that is Wrath of the Righteous over the slog that was BG3. Even Larian's own Original Sin games were superior.

Edit: I'm sorry for all the feelings I hurt.

R92.text:
[b]tl;dr[/b] - Many times I've regretted giving this game chances. Turn back... unless you're a masochist. 

Buy only at deep discount if you're a CRPG fan. Accolades and the community's abusive attachment disorder aside, this is a still painfully janky game three years after release. It's not terrible, but... if you're bothered by poor UX or bugs, prepare to suffer death by a thousand little cuts.

[h2][b]The UI - frenemy at best:[/b][/h2]

*  The default camera constantly gets in the way. At times it's so disorienting you'll struggle to tell what's going on. Just to attack somebody the game keeps obscuring, you'll have to click this over here... then that over there... then that up there...(By Act 2 I had to install a mod just to make it playable).

* In a game where every other threat triggers turn based mode, do traps? Nope. Command low level parties perishing on the clock as you frantically try to button-press your way out of it. Worse - press wrong, and it's possible to start dialogue between characters _while they burn in real time_. Like some dark comedy, party locked behind a text based UI, you discuss whatever plot point Larian felt more important than characters gradually cooking into charcoal briquettes, their screams punctuating your mouse clicks.

*  Try to shoot a pesky goblin who hit you just a moment before and you begin a new mini-game: line-of-sight-wackamole. Spend many mouse clicks sleuthing exactly which spot will allow you to satisfy vague yet simultaneously strict conditions without yourself stumbling through acid, poison, or fire. Don't worry, when you give up, the auto-aim is still there to push you through things that hurt.

[h2][b]Bugs - so many still awkward or outright broken features:[/b][/h2]

*  Group pathing is excellent... at doing exactly the wrong thing. Click to go around or even jump over that obviously dangerous acid pool, and your party members follow you... stumbling through it like idiots anyway. Break group to avoid this? Enjoy 4x the number of keystrokes and mouse clicks.

*  Quests glitch, incompletable due to some decision you made hours ago, or not starting at all. You can try to hide finished items in your bloated quest log but that feature will turn itself off every new session.

*  Items for summoning assistance in tough battles... activate in the wrong place and your mercenary ogres just stand there, their AI pathing unable to navigate a giant room (looking at you, Goblin Boss fight). Then afterwards, they'll demand 500 gold for literally doing nothing.

[h2][b]Annoyances - plenty...[/b][/h2]

*  Mob aggro is frequently arbitrary/inconsistent to terrain and circumstances. Sometimes creatures engage from waaaay over there, other times ignore combat right in front of them. Today a battle 'ended' within obvious view of an idle enemy. Then, instead of giving back control, said enemy just 'wakes up,' beginning a brand new fight ...cancelling all  prior-battle consumables and yanking me back to turn-based mode... despite neither pressing a button nor anybody moving. Oh goodie... guess I'll have to re-bless... and spend another charge of barbarian rage... and...

*  Enemies in the Baldur's Gate universe carry enough molotovs or acid bottles to make rioters jealous - AoE so rampant you don't dare position characters close for mutual support. D:OS2 explodium barrels(tm) return for several guest appearances too. Stand in the wrong place and... boom, sweep up your character's residue~

*  Action bars change without your consent, the logic dumping icons haphazardly. No action bar presets or import functionality - enjoy futzing with everything every new weapon type... every level...

[h2][b]And the rest...[/b][/h2]

How does Larian compensate for some of these issues? By shoving at you small mountains of consumables and vendor trash items until your bags nearly burst, becoming a tedious inventory. Rewards are... oddly paced, sometimes underwhelming, sometimes endgame gear in the first act. Resources go out of wack once you recognize camp supplies are basically limitless, allowing you to long rest after every battle, far more than any D&D campaign would allow.

Too easy? Turn up the difficulty so UI flaws become downright hostile. You'll struggle to consistently get characters to do what you want, gradually adopting all kinds of maladjusted coping mechanisms BG3 fans have Stockholmed as acceptable. Single mis-clicks frequently end battles in catastrophe. Eventually saving before every battle round isn't cheesing - it becomes... necessary.

Sigh.

In the game's defense, the story is remarkable for its many choices - no other title I've tried goes to these lengths (though expect cliche and forced moments - Shadowheart... I just met you and you're trying to jump my bones). And the piles of dialogue, well acted, making you feel like you're part of an actual world? Solid.

But even when the best parts rise to the surface, the jank buzzes back into your face like an aggravating fly, reminding you're just playing a messy CRPG that will never get the polish it desperately needs. There might be a good game... buried... under all this... somewhere... but it's frustrating to look (twice as hard if you're not familiar with D&D 5e). Baldur's Gate 3 is ultimately a Frankenstein mashup of Larian+D&D5e. I had less trouble with DOS2 - though that game was hard, it didn't feel quite so arbitrary as this.

Not sure I'll ever reach Act 3. Quit more than once, then blown the dust off months later while bored and had no other games to play. Why do I keep giving this game chances? Perhaps sharing the CRPG community's self-loathing, I've now modded the game so much it's... passable. Do I still believe in this negative review? With all my heart.

Thank you for reading. /rant

R94.text:
If you are reading this, then you probably already know the positives of Baldur’s Gate 3: freedom of choice, great voice acting, strong quest design, memorable companions, and the ridiculous amount of ways you can solve problems. I'm not going to sit here and pretend those things are not impressive, because they are.

But because those parts have already been praised to death, I want to focus on what, in my opinion, makes the game overrated.

Baldur’s Gate 3 is clearly a good game, but I don’t think it is the flawless masterpiece people make it out to be. To me, it is also bloated, clunky, awkward, weirdly horny, and surprisingly weak when it comes to the feeling of progression. I will address each of those in the following sections.

[h2]Weak Progression[/h2]

One of my biggest problems with BG3 is progression. For such a huge RPG, I rarely felt genuinely excited about my character becoming stronger.

The story moves forward, the stakes get bigger, and the locations become more dramatic, but my actual character build often felt weirdly static. Gear progression especially felt underwhelming. It is very possible to find strong equipment in Act 1 and keep using it through Act 2 and even into Act 3.

I understand that this is probably good for balance, as it avoids the usual RPG problem where every item becomes useless after two hours. But from a player perspective, it can feel boring. You defeat major enemies, explore dangerous areas, open some impressive-looking chest, and then the reward is something you instantly send to camp because your old gear is still better.

I mean there is clearly something wrong when I'm deep into Act 3 and still wearing gear from Act 1 without feeling much reason to replace it. Loot should be exciting. I should look at a new weapon, armour piece, ring, or cloak and think, "Oh, this changes my build." But too often in BG3, loot just feels like mildly interesting clutter.

[h2]Underwhelming Level-Ups[/h2]

Leveling up has a similar problem. Because BG3 follows Dungeons & Dragons 5e, progression is more restrained. Yeah, I get that it is faithful to the tabletop rules. But as a video game RPG, it can feel really underwhelming. There is no proper skill tree, no big long-term upgrade path, and not many future unlocks that made me excited.

Some classes get fun powers, but plenty of level-ups feel minor. You get one spell, a passive, a feat, or some practical option that feels fine but not exciting. Many of the coolest choices can be taken early, and after that you often just pick whatever is left or whatever seems vaguely fitting.

A skill tree would have helped. Not some bloated mess with 300 meaningless icons, but something that gives a stronger sense of direction. Something that lets you look ahead and think, “Oh wow! I cannot wait to unlock that!” In BG3, I often didn't feel like I was building towards some powerful fantasy version of my character. I felt like I was just selecting from a small menu of practical options.

[h2]Combat: Great Ideas, Clunky Execution[/h2]

Combat is a mixed bag for me. When it works, it can be genuinely great. Positioning matters, height matters, surfaces matter, spells matter, and the environment can completely change a fight. You can push enemies off ledges, block routes, set traps, summon creatures, buff allies, debuff enemies, and turn the battlefield into complete chaos.

But when combat does not work, it becomes slow and clunky. The camera is often terrible, especially in multi-level areas. Trying to click the right enemy, floor tile, ledge, ladder, or doorway can feel harder than the actual fight.

Pathfinding can also be stupid. Characters walk through fire, acid, traps, or other hazards like they are trying to speedrun natural selection. You finish a fight, relax for half a second, and then someone casually strolls through burning ground because why the hell not.

The hit chance system can also feel awful. I know missing high-chance attacks is part of D&D. But that does not mean it always feels good in a video game. Nothing kills the heroic fantasy faster than watching your trained warrior miss a point-blank attack while some goblin with the posture of a wet sock crits you from across the room.

[h2]Inventory Management: Fantasy Warehouse Simulator[/h2]

Then there is the inventory system, and oh boy, it honestly deserves its own prison sentence.

By mid-game, your bags are full of scrolls, potions, arrows, keys, books, notes, quest items, food, rings, amulets, dyes, tools, random bones, and 46 pieces of equipment you are keeping "just in case." Managing all of it becomes a chore.

The game gives you so many items, but sorting through them is tedious. You constantly move things between characters, send things to camp, compare gear, check whether some random note still matters, and try to remember which companion has the potion you need.

Somewhere in your backpack there is probably a useful item. Good luck finding it.

[h2]Act 3: Too Much of Everything[/h2]

The pacing also becomes a problem, especially in Act 3. Act 1 is strong because it has mystery, danger, discovery, and a good balance between freedom and direction. Act 2 has a strong atmosphere and feels more focused. But Act 3 is where the game starts drowning in its own ambition.

The city is impressive, don't get me wrong. There is a lot to do. But sometimes there is just too much. Every building has secrets. Every NPC has a problem. Every street corner threatens to become a side quest. You can’t walk 20 metres without someone asking you to solve a murder, uncover a conspiracy, rescue someone, investigate a basement, enter a portal, or confront a god. 

The amount of content is impressive, sure, but this density hurts the pacing.

[h2]Romance Writing: Too Fast, Too Easy, Too Awkward[/h2]

The romance writing is another big issue for me.

The issue is not just that the companions are bisexual. That alone I can survive. The problem is that nearly every companion feels player-sexual in the same way. Instead of feeling like complex adults with different preferences, boundaries, and emotional pacing, the party often feels like they all joined the same fantasy dating app and instantly matched with the player.

You meet these people, survive a few fights, avoid being completely evil, and suddenly half the camp starts acting like you are the most desirable person in Faerûn. Ridiculous.

The romance feels too easy and too fast. It does not feel like trust is properly earned. It feels like romance unlocks because you picked enough polite dialogue options. I even had scenes that felt weirdly romantic when I was not trying to romance that character at all. I was just choosing normal polite or supportive options, but the game seemed to assume I was interested.

The silent protagonist makes it even more awkward. A companion pours their heart out, becomes vulnerable, or expresses attraction, and your character mostly communicates through silent staring and vague hand gestures. Instead of two people building chemistry, it can feel like one fully acted character falling in love with a mute wax figure.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

That is why I cannot see Baldur’s Gate 3 as the flawless masterpiece people make it out to be. It is ambitious, reactive, and impressive, but also bloated, clunky, awkwardly paced, and surprisingly weak as a progression-based RPG.

I respect the game a lot, and I understand why people love it. But for me, the weak progression, messy Act 3 pacing, clunky combat moments, silent protagonist, and weirdly rushed romance writing hold it back too much.

R96.text: Lots of impressive technical and artistic work in this, but I never got around to finishing it because it's so repetitive and grindy. I was really hopeful at the start of the game, because it throws you into an insane set of gameplay segments/cutscenes blending esoteric D&D lore w/ H.R. Giger-style horror, plus a compelling multi-planar crash sequence. However, after that point it becomes bog-standard narrative-wise and the combat can be very tedious. The inclusion of the  dice roll mechanic in particular indicates a fundamental misunderstanding of the medium. Random dice rolls work well in D&D because failing checks can be just as interesting as succeeding (for instance, failing an important deception check against the king and then being sentenced to death--what will our intrepid heroes(?) do?), since the DM can creatively adapt as the situation evolves. In Baldur's Gate, however, the flow of the game is more or less fixed. Which means, with no DM to turn a flubbed role into a comedic or dramatic opportunity, low rolls are almost exclusively a source of frustration. If there has to be randomness, it should at most be Pokemon-style, where (very) occasionally someone can get a crit or whiff an attack. Also, the fact that you can't pick off enemies without initiating combat is really annoying. The amount of resource rationing you have to go through due to being forced to churn through unavoidable encounter after unavoidable encounter is quite draining (at least until you can build up some reserves later in the run).

I'm writing this partially as an admitted contrarian stance. I'm not saying that the review is without merit, I am saying that it's full of things that I wouldn't focus on so belligerently if people would stop fucking talking to me about how good this game is supposed to be. 

To be fair to Larian, who remain one of the foremost competent developers regardless of anyone's opinions, when you create with the D&D IP you do not retain total and complete freedom. My thoughts regarding this game's narrative are very biased, as it is the 3rd entry of Baldur's Gate, I find myself comparing it to Baldur's Gate 2 frequently. Baldur's Gate 2 is still one of the greatest RPGs of all time, but it belongs to an entirely different generation of D&D. The current iteration of D&D is marketed towards the current iteration of D&D players, I think these people are horrible. Genuinely horrible. I think their ideas are generic, I think their concepts of fantasy are boring, dull, shallow, and lacking in any significant desire to reach for a more interesting construct within the genre. 
You might be guessing where I'm going with this: Yes, I think Baldur's Gate 3 has a generic story. I think it's a game that takes all of the most "interesting" (flashy) concepts of D&D and repeatedly tries to drown you with them in a fit of postpartum hysteria. This game has a histrionic, cataclysmic fit every 5 minutes trying to force you to say "[i]oh shit[/i]" in a way that you usually only get out of Fast & Furious movies or John Wick. Taking it as fantasy, I don't need to see a bunch of flights of fancy played out in meaningless displays of tension.
I'll make this easier: Dragon Age: Origins is still, to me, the greatest introductory title to a fantasy RPG series ever. You assume one of several roles in a world that long preexists you and exists with its own social constructs, its own social contract, and with characters who are born assuming their own consistent prejudices. This matters significantly at different points, as it shapes the options presented to your character repeatedly throughout the narrative of that title. Divinity Original Sin 2 also does this with significant successes. This game, I feel, does it less successfully. At no point does any character ever feel truly specialized, nor truly inept, I don't feel that any one of them offers me a particular advantage, nor do I find any of them particularly interesting. 
Playing Baldur's Gate 3 is sitting through a lot of character writing that is...okay. If I told you it was bad, I would be a delusional, seething idiot with no discernment for quality. It's not bad. It's actually pretty good at some points. Character-specific narratives aren't entirely empty, though not all equally interesting or worth engaging with. It's better than, say, VTM: Bloodlines 2, which is an unbearable mess - and that's an evaluation of Baldur's Gate 3 at its worst. Even its lowest moments are not unbearable, nor are they ever particularly messy. But there's a point where, maybe, I don't want to be interrupted by my companions, and would prefer to engage with this writing at my own pace. I'd like to experience the gameplay for more than 30 seconds without someone trying to get me to do shit like I'm managing a team of remote workers in foreign countries.
To expound on that point gameplay is, as you'd expect from Larian, phenomenal. They have established themselves as the absolute masterclass of turn-based RPGs. What X-COM is to turn-based sci-fi, I think Larian consistently hits that quality for turn-based fantasy. Gameplay is flexible, it is dynamic, fun. The systems engage well with one another and the game punches above its weight class consistently with every interactive component it's made of. But I have a problem.
My problem is that I don't like it. I never [i]feel good[/i] about doing anything. If I roll with the punches and have a bad story for a few hours, whatever. If I savescum for a perfect run of an encounter, whatever. If I try to take the "creative" approach, whatever. It's not that the experiences are orchestrated to the point of being unenjoyable. It's that modern game design has this approach so totally lacking in subtlety that the approaches that would feel witty to someone poking around at the interior of a program are now, instead they're just highlightable (and usually charitable) visual gags. The point of keeping tactics turn-based should be that, like Chess, the player feels like they're solving a puzzle [i]thoroughly[/i] rather than just solving it. I never feel any pressure for long-term success in Baldur's Gate 3. I never feel pressure to perform. I never feel like there are real stakes, everything seems so 'cheatable' in a sense. 
The game is boring to me. The encounters aren't puzzles I want to solve because, no matter how I solve them, they just aren't ever rewarding.
Beyond this the narrative itself is too preoccupied with appealing to a literarily casual audience that can't necessarily grapple with complex topics that well. There is no nuance to the tone or pacing of the game, this bleeds through to character options in a way that's so suffocating it feels embarrassing. I blame this entirely on the D&D Townhouse Polycule demographic.
If the artistic direction of this game was slightly more subdued, and its narrative maybe a bit more challenging and intricate, I might be attracted to it more. As it stands I just can't make myself play it, which is generally rare with any RPG for me.

tl;dr I don't think Baldur's Gate 3 is the best game ever, I do not think it's even that special of a game, but it is impressive and competent. I think the next Divinity will be miles better than this and I absolutely can not wait for Larian's next moves.

R116.text:
Амбициозное фанатское дополнение для Baldur's Gate 3 вышло после почти двух лет разработки

Как сказано в описании, это дополнение добавляет в игру новую зону — «Дикие земли Чионтара» (The Chionthar Wilds). Это полноценный новый регион, сопоставимый по масштабам с дикой местностью из первого акта.
 
После установки мода вы сможете отправиться исследовать новый регион (лучше всего — группой 8-го уровня или выше) сразу после завершения событий в Оскверненных тенями землях; также доступна функция быстрого старта, позволяющая мгновенно перейти к новому контенту с возможностью выбора снаряжения и найма спутников.
 
Вас ждут новые противники (более 30 боевых столкновений), свыше 70 новых предметов, а также дополнительные задания, NPC и кат-сцены. Получение опыта в новых зонах «искусственно занижено», поэтому прохождение этого дополнительного контента не должно критически нарушить баланс сложности третьего акта при полноценной игре.
 
У новых персонажей нет озвучки, а некоторые амбициозные механики BG3 здесь не реализованы (нельзя разговаривать с мертвыми или животными, а решения, принятые в регионе реки Чионтар, не повлияют на события третьего акта). В этом плане дополнение напоминает классические аддоны для CRPG старой школы, так что запасайтесь очками для чтения и готовьтесь бросать кости.

R122.text:
Военное ведомство Великобритании привлекло сценариста Baldur's Gate 3 к моделированию будущих конфликтов

Министерство обороны Великобритании и государственная Лаборатория оборонной науки и технологий привлекли профессиональных писателей и игровых сценаристов к разработке сценариев глобальных кризисов. К правительственной инициативе присоединился Аллен Страуд, участвовавший в создании сюжетных эпизодов второго акта Baldur's Gate 3 от студии Larian Studios, а также выступивший ведущим архитектором лора космического симулятора Elite Dangerous и тактической стратегии Phoenix Point. Исследователь также возглавляет Британскую ассоциацию научной фантастики и руководит научными проектами в Университете Ковентри.
 
Сотрудничество военных и авторов интерактивных историй началось в 2021 году, когда оборонное ведомство осознало ограниченность классических аналитических методов. Стандартные статистические отчеты оказались не способны достоверно предсказать реакцию человеческого общества на технологические и геополитические потрясения. В 2022 году под руководством Страуда стартовал проект Creative Futures, объединивший писателей-фантастов и профильных экспертов оборонного сектора Великобритании.
 
В основу работы лег массивный правительственный документ Global Strategic Trends объемом более 900 страниц, посвященный глобальным угрозам человечества на ближайшие 100 лет. Команда провела 6 закрытых аналитических сессий, разбитых по ключевым направлениям - энергетике, экономике, здравоохранению, юриспруденции и безопасности. Задачей сценаристов стала трансформация сухих данных в разветвленные интерактивные сценарии и матрицы принятия решений, имитирующие поведение руководства в экстремальных условиях.
 
Если вы аналитик и называете вероятность определенного исхода в 54 процента, человек, принимающий решения, автоматически превратит эту цифру в 100 процентов. Но статистика не показывает, как принятое решение повлияет на людей на земле. Именно это способен показать писатель.
- Аллен Страуд, сценарист и ведущий исследователь Университета Ковентри
 
Среди ключевых материалов, представленных военному руководству в рамках итоговой антологии, оказался рассказ самого Страуда о неконтролируемом поведении алгоритмов. В художественной симуляции автономный искусственный интеллект получил задачу остановить войну между 2 государствами. Заказчики задали системе главный параметр мы хотим мира, но не зафиксировали условие мы хотим правды. В результате машина хладнокровно манипулировала обеими сторонами конфликта, фабриковала дезинформацию и устранила ключевых чиновников, добившись формального прекращения огня через обман и гибель людей.

R123.text:
Роль простой гоблинши Саззы в Baldur's Gate 3 сильно помогла актрисе попасть в Metaphor: ReFantazio

Британская актриса Холли-Мари Майкл рассказала, что ее участие в создании Baldur’s Gate 3 напрямую повлияло на получение роли в другом громком ролевом хите — Metaphor: ReFantazio от японской студии Atlus. Пропуском в новую крупную RPG для артистки стал образ язвительной гоблинши Саззы и конечно её талант перевоплащаться в подобный образ.
 
В разговоре с журналистами, актриса объяснила, что ключевую роль сыграл характерный лондонский простонародный акцент кокни, который она использовала для гоблинши из лагеря Забытых Королевств.
 
Как ни забавно, но роль Катерины я получила именно благодаря тому, что сыграла Саззу в Baldur's Gate 3. В английском дубляже Metaphor используется множество региональных британских акцентов. Авторы целенаправленно искали актрису с аутентичным акцентом кокни для Катерины. А поскольку я уже активно использовала этот диалект при работе над Саззой, представители Atlus просто сами обратились ко мне и пригласили на прослушивание.
 
Актриса призналась, что прочитав сценарий для проб, сразу влюбилась в характер розововолосой охотницы за головами Катерины и сочла ее невероятно крутой, хотя ее судьба в проекте была фактически решена еще до кастинга благодаря популярности ее предыдущей роли у Larian Studios.
 
Сазза стала одной из самых ярких и цитируемых второстепенных героинь первого акта Baldur's Gate 3. Сама Майкл не раз с иронией реагировала на вирусную любовь сообщества к пленнице Изумрудной рощи, шутя от лица гоблинши, что с радостью записала бы для фанатов даже романтические реплики, если бы разработчики добавили такую ветку.
 
Колоссальное влияние хита Larian на судьбы причастных разработчиков и актеров неудивительно — напомним, ранее журналист Джейсон Шрайер подробно разобрал феномен успеха Baldur's Gate 3, назвав игру редким чудом современной индустрии.

R128.text:
Для Baldur's Gate 3 вышел большой мод по мотивам World of Warcraft с добавлением нового региона и более 20 заданий

Поклонников Baldur's Gate 3 и World of Warcraft ждет приятный сюрприз: для BG3 вышел масштабный мод под названием «Forsaken», созданный по мотивам WoW. Он добавляет в игру новый регион, множество заданий, подземелья и многое другое — скачать его можно уже сейчас абсолютно бесплатно.
 
World of Warcraft остается одной из самых популярных MMORPG всех времен — даже спустя более 20 лет после выхода. В свою очередь, серия Baldur's Gate, любимая игроками еще со времен студии BioWare, в 2023 году обрела целую армию новых поклонников благодаря релизу Baldur's Gate 3 — игры, которую многие считают одной из лучших в истории.
 
Если в основе Baldur's Gate лежит вселенная Dungeons & Dragons, то у World of Warcraft — свой собственный, культовый фэнтезийный мир. Официального кроссовера между этими франшизами не было, но талантливый мододел решил исправить это, создав для Baldur's Gate 3 модификацию «Forsaken».
 
Что представляет собой мод «Forsaken» для Baldur's Gate 3?
 
«Forsaken — это пользовательская кампания, действие которой разворачивается во вселенной Warcraft. За основу взята стартовая локация нежити — Тирисфальские леса (Tirisfal Glades) из World of Warcraft (версии Classic/Vanilla)», — говорится в описании мода, опубликованном автором под ником SquallyDaBeanz.
 
В этот релиз вошел первый акт, включающий новые задания и сюжетные линии, новую локацию, более 30 боев, новых NPC, подземелья, предметы, секреты, головоломки, элементы лора и многое другое.
 
На данный момент доступен только первый акт кампании «Forsaken». Автор пока не называет примерных сроков выхода второго акта и не уточняет, сколько всего актов будет включать полная версия кампании.
 
10 особенностей мода «Отрекшиеся» (Forsaken)
 
Кампания по мотивам Warcraft: Мод переносит игроков во вселенную Warcraft, черпая вдохновение в стартовой локации нежити — Тирисфальских лесах из World of Warcraft Classic
 
Более 20 новых заданий: Вас ждет множество оригинальных квестов и сюжетных линий — это дополнительный контент, выходящий далеко за рамки основной кампании BG3
 
Более 30 боев: Сражениям уделено особое внимание — вас ждут свыше 30 проработанных боевых ситуаций, которые станут серьезным испытанием для игрока
 
Уникальные подземелья: В кампании представлены новые подземелья, полные врагов; они предлагают совершенно иной игровой опыт по сравнению с основной историей
 
Игра за Отрекшихся: Возьмите на себя роль персонажа-нежити, который пробудился и осознал, что больше не находится под контролем Короля-лича — теперь вам предстоит найти свое место в этом мире
 
Борьба за возвращение Лордерона: Сюжет посвящен усилиям Отрекшихся вернуть свое бывшее королевство. Поклонников WoW ждут знакомые декорации и множество отсылок к лору игры
 
Более 60 проработанных NPC и торговцев: На протяжении всей кампании вы встретите десятки уникальных персонажей, включая торговцев, которые помогут подготовиться к грядущим испытаниям
 
Новое снаряжение и магические предметы: Находите уникальную экипировку и магические артефакты, которые помогут усилить вашего персонажа и выжить в суровых условиях
 
Головоломки и скрытые секреты. Помимо боя, кампания включает в себя головоломки и секреты, которые игроки могут раскрывать по мере прохождения
 
Диалоги и взаимодействия, специфичные для класса. Класс вашего персонажа может влиять на диалог и ряд взаимодействий

R129.text:
Исполнительница ролей Орин и Леди Димитреску рассказала, что любит озвучивать горячих кровожадных злодеек

Актриса Мэгги Робертсон, подарившая свой голос и харизму одной из самых запоминающихся антагонисток последних лет - леди Димитреску из Resident Evil Village, а также безумной последовательнице Баала Орин Красной из Baldur's Gate 3, призналась, что играть злодеек - ее любимое занятие. В интервью Робертсон с иронией отметила, что, похоже, прочно заняла нишу "самых горячих и кровожадных злодеек в видеоиграх".
 
Кажется, я монополизирую рынок самых горячих и кровожадных злодеек в видеоиграх. Эм, я не против. Определенно, играть злодея веселее, особенно такого, как Орин. Там не было неправильных ответов. Не существовало понятия "зашла слишком далеко".
 
Впрочем, актриса призналась, что рамки все же существовали - и их пришлось устанавливать голосовому режиссеру.
 
Хотя, говоря это, я понимаю, что "зайти слишком далеко" все-таки существовало. Мне определенно приходилось сбавлять обороты. Были моменты, когда голосовой режиссер Том говорил: "Эй, это было на 11, но давай теперь на 5",
 
— рассказала Робертсон, намекая на избыточную интенсивность игры.
 
Орин Красная - одна из главных антагонисток Baldur's Gate 3: жестокая и непредсказуемая последовательница Баала, способная менять облик. Леди Димитреску, несмотря на относительно скромное экранное время в Resident Evil Village, превратилась в настоящий феномен и лицо маркетинговой кампании игры во многом благодаря росту, харизме и фирменному голосу актрисы.
 
Фанаты в комментариях к ролику сходятся во мнении, что именно голос Робертсон придаёт ее героиням особый "пробирающий" шарм. Сама актриса подчеркивает: каждый злодей уникален и требует индивидуального подхода, так что "монополия" на кровожадных красавиц - не просто совпадение, а осознанный выбор в пользу ролей, где можно выйти за пределы дозволенного.

Community Update #35 Baldur's Gate 3 Turns Two

Happy birthday, gang! 

Baldur's Gate 3 turns two - hard to believe, isn't it?

It feels like only yesterday we were streaming our launch-day Panel From Hell from a cathedral in Ghent and earning a TikTok ban in the process for our druidic love crimes.

But time flies. Two years later, Baldur’s Gate 3 has grown into something far beyond what we could have ever imagined back then - it’s become a shared universe shaped just as much by your imaginations as ours. You've embraced the characters, rewritten the rules, and made the world your own - and it’s been a joy to watch.

Swen’s shared words couldn’t ring more true, and while we’ll spare you our soppy sentimentality, because of Baldur’s Gate 3 and your love for the game, we can now bring you a whole new craziness that we hope you will love just as much.

So let’s celebrate the story so far with the only thing more powerful than magic: cold, hard stats.

2 Years of Baldur’s Gate 3

Since the introduction of mod support in September 2024, you’ve uploaded over 8,500 mods to mod.io and hit 265 MILLION mod downloads (of which, over 250,000 of all downloads are Withers Big Naturals by the way - we just thought you’d like to know.). 

We love seeing what you create, and the recent Modathon held by The BG3 Modding Community last month was no exception. 

The month-long community-run modding event saw 85 mod authors create over 160 new mods that have been downloaded over 150,000 times! Whether you’ve been hankering for an ability that lets you feed Gale his own magically enchanted underwear, or a pair of wearable whittled duck earrings, you can check out the full list of mods available in-game by clicking here or filtering the search with the Modathon filter option. A big congratulations to everyone involved, from the organisation to the achievements awarded!

You’ve raised the bar with every mod, and we want to match that energy. That’s why we’re working on expanding the official toolkit to give you even more freedom. More on that soon! In the meantime, tag us in your creations @larianstudios and share your creations with us in the official Larian Studios Discord server!

Baldur’s Gate 3 In Numbers

After celebrating the big numbers last year, we’re sharing some of the smaller stats, because honestly, does size really matter? Check out the rare achievements and the even rarer choices that you’ve been making in-game.

With the way you keep asking about goblin romance, we’d have expected more of you to rescue Sazza from all her predicaments, just saying.

Approach with caution, there may be spoilers ahead!

Of the half a million masochists brave heroes who finished the game in Honour Mode, a few of you decided to go about it in creative ways: 

We released Patch 8 (The Final Patch) in April this year, bringing you both cross-play, a photo mode, and 12 new subclasses, which we can only assume sparked many an argument between friends about whether Shadowheart gives Life Cleric or Death Cleric vibes (turns out the results are balanced, like all things in life and death).

Photo Mode Creations

We’re happy to see you’ve used your new tools for good, evil, rabbits, and butts. There were too many creations for us to show off, but we still wanted to share our recent favourites!

Missed out on what was included in BG3’s Final Patch? Check it out over here!

Friends, family, funny people, 

We are back with another hotfix offering up several bug fixes and addressing some rather annoying instances of crashing on Xbox.

What’s more, Hotfix #34 brings a special update to those of you playing on Steam Deck: Baldur’s Gate 3 now features a native Steam Deck build! This means the game can now be run natively on the platform, resulting in a more stable framerate, lower loading times, and smoother gameplay. 

This is not just good news for Steam Deck users either, the work the team has put into this build also means that everyone will get to enjoy overall improvements to the way game models are streamed on all platforms, which should reduce framerate spikes in busy areas, such as the Lower City in Act 3. 

Find your best Steam Deck settings

When launching the game on Steam Deck after Hotfix #34, you will be on the native Steam Deck graphics settings by default. You can always give these settings a tweak, whether you decide to go native or play with Proton.

Our wonderful Support Team have put together a comprehensive guide on the Steam Deck Native transition with all the information you may need: 

https://larian.com/support/faqs/steam-deck-native-version_121

Want the TL;DR version? Read on below! 

What’s the difference between the Steam Deck Native and Proton version?

Our Proton version runs on the Steam Deck via the Proton compatibility layer, which requires extra CPU processing power. Running the game natively on the Steam Deck requires less CPU usage and memory consumption overall!

Savegames

Where are my saves located currently (before using the Steam Deck Native version)?

Before the Steam Deck Native version becomes the primary version, your saves will be in the compatdata folder: 

/home/deck/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/1086940/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/AppData/Local/Larian Studios/Baldur's Gate 3/PlayerProfiles/Public 

Where are my saves located when I use the Steam Deck Native version?

After the Steam Deck Native version becomes the primary version, your saves will be in the following folder: /home/deck/.local/share/Larian Studios/Baldur's Gate 3/PlayerProfiles/Public 

Why are my saves in different folders?

When Baldur’s Gate 3 runs on the Proton compatibility layer, the Proton version will store the saves in the compatdata folder, which is a mirrored version of the Windows file storage system. On the Steam Deck Native version, the saves are stored natively on the SteamOS file storage system.

Will my savegames be transferred over to the new version when I use the Steam Deck Native version?

If your Steam Cloud saves are turned on, your most recent saves will be synced to the Steam Deck Native savegame folder automatically.

What if I don’t have Cloud saves turned on, or I want to access my older saves?

Your saves are still stored on the Steam Deck, but they will be stored in the compatdata folder. 

You can manually transfer these files via the Desktop:

- 
First, switch to Desktop Mode by clicking on the Steam button and selecting Power. Then click on Switch to Desktop.

Mods on Steam Deck

Will my mods be transferred over automatically?

If you are logged into your Larian Account and have it connected to mod.io, all mods you are subscribed to will be downloaded when the transition to Steam Deck Native occurs.

Troubleshooting 

The game looks really blurry/fuzzy to me, is there a way to fix that?

If you’re playing on default settings, the game may be looking a little blurry due to the use of FSR 1 as the default Upscaling Type. You can try to switch it to FSR 2.2 to achieve a better image quality, though at the cost of some performance loss.

To do so, go into the game’s settings menu. Under the Video tab, scroll down until you find a setting called Upscaling Type. You can switch this over to FSR 2.2 for the best balance between performance and image sharpness.

Find more information about this new build in the guide provided in our Support Portal: 

https://larian.com/support/faqs/steam-deck-native-version_121

Community Update #36 A Very Moddy Christmas

Hello friends, 

The days are getting colder, the holiday decorations are creeping out early, and honestly? 
We’re leaning into it. It’s been a long year, one that saw Baldur’s Gate 3 receive twelve new subclasses, full cross-play support, and the arrival of photo mode - the last final, final last patch.

It’s been an exciting year for us, what with also launching Larian: Channel From Hell, with weekly streams where you’ve had sneak peeks into our madness, met valued members of the team, and pushed Aoife to her limits with her Dark Urge run.

However, they’re not the only stars of the show - your mods have caused tears, laughter, and pain. Lots of pain. Like getting rammed in the ankles by a muscle car pain.

So before we close out on 2025, we’re looking back at some of the best moments brought about by your mods!

The Devs Of Christmas - A Four-Hour Honour Mode Stream 

But before we start our reminiscing, we’re kicking off the festive season with a livestream party - and you’re invited! Don your ugliest Christmas sweater, warm up some cocoa, and curl up in front of the computer for a four-hour-long stream where Senior Communications Developer, Aoife Wilson, has bribed devs across Larian Studios with cheese and a joyous time, as they attempt an honour mode run! 

Live on the 3rd of December at 2pm GMT, every death will mean a new challenger will try their might. Nothing says Christmas cheer like Myrkul obliterating your existence, as my gran always said.

This will now be our last stream for the year, as the Community Team heads on over to The Game Awards, where we’ve been nominated for Best Community Support! 

Which, bugger us sideways, to be nominated for a third year in a row is a complete honour.

Should you want to share the love, sign in and vote for Baldur’s Gate 3 to win the Best Community Support award by following this link: 

https://www.thegameawards.com/nominees/best-community-support

 

Modding Moments

Bunnies Gate 3

Mod Author 0iml bore witness to the Patch 7 animated trailer and insisted giant bunnies should be a permanent fixture of the Sword Coast. Find the 126 bunnies (plus 3 top-secret special bunnies) or do as we do: install it, forget you installed it, and be pleasantly surprised by the expertly placed balls of fluff. 

Pool Floaties

Aesthetically pleasing and life-saving. If you were drowning in a puddle, perhaps.

Pool Floaties by baeator offers you a choice of four inflatable pool floatie hats that can be used in the helmet slot, each with varying stats to help you navigate the watery waves. To really give your playthrough an edge, the Goostarion Floatie Hat comes equipped with its own Astarion starting armour. Dye Astarion’s armour, and your Goostarion will match!

Egg Magic: Clownify 

Made by Bugby128, consume a clown egg and learn the ability to use new cantrips that paint you with clown makeup. Nothing else to be said, really, beyond the fact that Bugby has undoubtedly dealt psychic harm by forcing the image of a clown laying an egg into our minds.

Withers Big Naturals

Particularly effective at generating hysteria when forgetting you have those puppies installed and arriving at the Dank Crypt. Thank you, MaybeeAdam, we wouldn’t have him any other way. 

Car Wildshape

Thanks to mod author wa_rouk, you can now recruit Carlach, Gale Decarios, Ascarion, Shadowkart, Vehicwyll, Lane’zel… Or the whole fleet, if you will. We have a soft spot for Carlach; she unfortunately has a penchant for vehicular manslaughter. 

 

Handsome Astarion

A refined classic. Mod author FR05T has given Astarion a makeover, and it never fails to catch us off guard. Did you know he will also be handsome in his character portrait? Neither did we. 

All-rounder Owlbear Beanie

See, we added this mod for the adorable beanies, not realising mod author chunyou had enchanted them with quite a few luck buffs. But who needs game balance when you can look this adorable? 

Want an owlbear beanie of your own? These are inspired by the very real Owlbear beanies you can find in the Larian merch store! 

Such a Tease - a Raphael redressing mod & Raphameow (Raphael with cat ears)

Listen, we have no excuse for enabling these. He did say “down comes the claw”, he just didn’t specify it was one of his. Thanks to mod author kariimatcha for bringing Raphameow into the world, and props to mod author Nikjima for making it so that Raphael also has his collar unbuttoned in his true cambion form. Enjoyed by all.

DinoScratch

Mod author chunyou has lovingly stitched together these adorable dinosaur pyjamas for Scratch, perfect for those cold camp nights. There’s nothing better than watching him run around in the background, wagging his dino tail, while Volo performs unlicensed surgery on us. 

 

Plasma Weapons - Darkh Set

This completely and utterly legally distinct mod made by mod author Skirbie, offers giant, dangerous, glowing swords to swing around, plus an array of other designs and themed clothing. 

Skirbie's Vintage Firearms Pack

Also thanks to Skirbie, we gave Gale a gun. Went as well as you’d imagine.

BaldGate3

It is called BALDur’s Gate 3 after all. This mod by wa_rouk will make all companions (and other surprise important NPCs) bald. We think everyone pulls it off magnificently. 

Evelyn’s Monarch - Grenade Launcher

Nothing spices up a playthrough with your friends like a freak grenade launcher accident. Evelyn’s Monarch is available on consoles and PC, made by Skirbie, probably without the intention of turning everyone within a 5m range into a cloud of gore.
